questions.stem: When is OSHA most likely to use the General Duty Clause?
options: Whenever an employer has any first-aid case
For a recognized serious hazard when no specific applicable standard addresses it and feasible abatement exists
Only when a state law is missing
To replace every specific OSHA standard
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Section 5(a)(1) addresses recognized hazards causing or likely to cause death or serious harm when the legal elements are met.
incorrectOptionExplanations: A minor case alone does not establish the elements of a General Duty Clause violation.
The clause is a federal duty and is not limited to missing state law.
Specific applicable standards are normally used when they address the hazard.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 4, General Duty Clause, pp. 56-57; OSH Act Section 5(a)(1)

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes horizontal and vertical OSHA standards?
options: Horizontal standards apply only to construction
Vertical standards always override federal law
Horizontal standards apply broadly; vertical standards apply to specified industries or operations
The terms describe whether a document is printed landscape or portrait
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A horizontal standard has broad industry application, while a vertical standard addresses a particular industry or type of work.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Construction-specific rules are examples of vertical coverage.
Applicability is determined by scope and industry, not by overriding the statute.
The terms describe regulatory applicability, not page orientation.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 4, horizontal and vertical standards, p. 56

questions.stem: After receiving an OSHA citation, how long must the employer generally post it at or near the violation?
options: One calendar day only
Fifteen working days only
Until the next annual audit
Three working days or until abatement, whichever is longer
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: The citation must remain posted for three working days or until the violation is abated, whichever is longer.
incorrectOptionExplanations: One day does not meet the posting duration.
Fifteen working days is associated with the contest period, not the posting rule.
Posting is tied to the specified period and abatement, not the audit schedule.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 4, OSHA citations, pp. 59-60; OSHA inspection guidance

questions.stem: How long does an employer generally have to submit a written Notice of Contest after receiving an OSHA citation and proposed penalty?
options: 15 working days
24 hours
7 calendar days
60 calendar days
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A written Notice of Contest must be submitted within 15 working days or the citation and proposed penalty become a final order.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Twenty-four hours applies to reporting certain severe events.
Seven days is associated with recordkeeping entry.
Sixty days exceeds the federal contest period.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 4, employer appeals and Notice of Contest, pp. 61-62

questions.stem: What must a workplace Hazard Communication program coordinate?
options: Medical examinations, exposure testing, and annual wellness-program participation for all employees
Inventory, labels, SDS access, training, and nonroutine or multi-employer communication
Fire-protection inspections, extinguisher servicing, evacuation drills, and emergency-alarm maintenance
Purchasing records, vendor invoices, chemical costs, and approval signatures for each ordered product
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: HazCom connects chemical classification and inventory with labels, safety data sheets, training, and workplace communication procedures.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Medical surveillance may be required by other standards but does not constitute the HazCom program.
Fire protection is separate from chemical hazard communication.
Purchase records do not provide the required hazard information and training system.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 4, Hazard Communication, pp. 63-66; OSHA 1910.1200(e)-(h)

questions.stem: Which SDS section should be consulted first for occupational exposure limits and recommended engineering controls and PPE?
options: Section 1, Identification
Section 5, Fire-fighting measures
Section 8, Exposure controls/personal protection
Section 14, Transport information
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Section 8 contains control parameters, exposure limits, engineering controls, and personal-protection information.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Section 1 identifies the product and supplier but is not the primary control section.
Section 5 addresses fire response and extinguishing information.
Section 14 focuses on transportation classification and precautions.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 4, Safety Data Sheet sections, pp. 65 and 116-121; OSHA 1910.1200 Appendix D

questions.stem: Why is pressing a machine stop button insufficient for lockout/tagout?
options: Stop buttons always remove stored energy
OSHA prohibits stopping machinery before lockout
A stop button is stronger than a disconnect switch
A control-circuit device does not physically isolate hazardous energy and may fail or be activated
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: LOTO requires use of energy-isolating devices, control of stored energy, and verification before servicing.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Stored and incoming energy require separate isolation and control.
Stopping equipment is part of preparation; the issue is that it is not energy isolation.
A disconnect or other energy-isolating device physically prevents energy transmission.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 4, control of hazardous energy, pp. 68-71; OSHA 1910.147

questions.stem: How often must the energy-control procedure be periodically inspected at a minimum?
options: At least annually
Every five years
Only after an injury
Every shift for every procedure
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: An authorized employee other than those using the procedure performs the periodic inspection at least annually and deviations are corrected.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Five years exceeds the required minimum interval.
The inspection is proactive and is not triggered only by injury.
Per-shift inspection is not the stated minimum periodic review requirement.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 4, periodic inspection, p. 70; OSHA 1910.147(c)(6)

questions.stem: Which oxygen concentrations define oxygen-deficient and oxygen-enriched atmospheres under the general-industry permit-space rule?
options: Less than 18% and more than 21%
Less than 19.5% and more than 23.5%
Less than 20% and more than 25%
Less than 10% and more than 90%
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: The rule defines oxygen deficiency below 19.5% by volume and oxygen enrichment above 23.5% by volume.
incorrectOptionExplanations: These values do not match the regulatory definitions.
These thresholds are not the definitions used by the rule.
These extreme values would miss serious hazardous atmospheres.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 4, confined-space definitions, pp. 71-73; OSHA 1910.146(b)

questions.stem: A permit-space program lists the local fire department as rescue without evaluating or coordinating with it. What is the main gap?
options: Naming any public agency automatically satisfies rescue planning
The attendant should enter alone for every rescue
The employer must evaluate rescue capability, response time, equipment, and availability and provide relevant access and information
Rescue planning is unnecessary when ventilation is used
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Rescue arrangements must be credible for the space and hazards, coordinated in advance, and supported by appropriate equipment and practice.
incorrectOptionExplanations: A listed service may be unavailable or incapable of the specific rescue.
An unplanned attendant entry can create multiple victims.
Ventilation can fail and does not control all permit-space hazards.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: OSHA 1910.146(d)(9) and (k); Yates Chapter 4, confined spaces

questions.stem: A vapor exposure exceeds the limit and feasible local exhaust can control it. What is the preferred approach?
options: Use respirators permanently and reject feasible engineering control
Rely only on odor to decide when protection is needed
Rotate more employees through the exposure
Implement the engineering control and use appropriate respirators while it is being installed or when needed for residual risk
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Occupational disease should be controlled as far as feasible by engineering measures, with a complete respiratory program where respirators are necessary.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The respiratory rule prioritizes feasible engineering controls over routine dependence on respirators.
Odor is not a reliable exposure or breakthrough indicator.
Rotation spreads exposure and is lower in the hierarchy.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 4, respiratory protection, pp. 75-77; OSHA 1910.134(a)

questions.stem: Before selecting PPE for a new task, what must the employer do?
options: Assess workplace hazards, select protective equipment that addresses them and fits the user, and document the assessment as required
Let each employee choose based only on preference
Purchase the least expensive PPE without task review
Use one PPE set for every hazard
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: PPE selection follows a documented hazard assessment and must provide safe design, suitability, communication, training, and proper fit.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Preference cannot replace hazard-based selection and employer responsibility.
Cost does not establish protection, compatibility, or fit.
Different hazards require different protection and may have incompatible equipment needs.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapters 4 and 14, PPE hazard assessment; OSHA 1910.132(d)
